model.note: Site does not publish a full API model string (e.g. claude-fable-5-YYYYMMDD); only the short id 'claude-fable-5'.

metric_definition.verbatim_unit_string_from_artifact: pass@1 is attempt pass rate over scored rollout attempts. pass@4 is tasks with at least one passing rollout divided by tasks attempted. Context-window failures and agent timeouts are scored failures; provider/verifier/network errors are excluded. Efficiency aggregates are over every scored attempt.
metric_definition.verbatim_scope_string_from_artifact: Every DeepSWE rollout across imported Pier jobs, grouped by configuration (harness + model + reasoning effort)
metric_definition.scale: fraction 0-1 (site renders as an integer percentage)
metric_definition.denominator: scored rollout ATTEMPTS, not tasks. 113 tasks x 4 whole-benchmark runs = 452 attempts per config; attempts excluded as provider/verifier/network errors are dropped from both numerator and denominator.
metric_definition.numerator: attempts whose committed git patch made the verifier report reward = 1.0 (all fail-to-pass AND all pass-to-pass task-defining tests green)
metric_definition.pass_at_4: tasks with at least one passing rollout / tasks attempted (denominator 113 tasks) - a per-task metric, NOT comparable to pass@1
metric_definition.failure_accounting: Context-window failures and agent timeouts count as scored FAILURES. Provider/verifier/network errors are EXCLUDED from scoring entirely.
metric_definition.ci_method: 95% run-to-run: SE across repeated whole-benchmark passes (1.96 * std(runs)/sqrt(R))
metric_definition.ci_caveat: This is a run-to-run standard error across 4 whole-benchmark passes, NOT a Wilson/binomial interval over tasks. Do not plot it interchangeably with a binomial CI from a local harness.
metric_definition.grading: Isolated verification: agent commits to a feature branch, the committed diff only is extracted and applied in a fresh verifier container which runs the tests and emits a CTRF report naming each task-defining test and its status. v1.1 grades by test node-id (v1 graded by process exit code).
metric_definition.cost_definition: mean_cost_usd = mean USD per scored attempt (whole task rollout), across all 4 runs. Includes input, cached-input and output tokens at provider list prices.
metric_definition.token_definition: mean_output_tokens / mean_input_tokens = mean tokens per scored attempt. Input token counts are cumulative across all agent steps, so they are very large (millions) and mostly cache reads; peak_context_tokens is the single-step context high-water mark.
metric_definition.row_selection_rule_for_displayed_number: The site runs each model at up to 5 reasoning_effort settings and, in its default 'Best' view, collapses them to one row per model by taking the HIGHEST available reasoning_effort (not the highest-scoring one). For claude-fable-5 that is 'max' (pass@1 0.6972), even though 'xhigh' scores marginally higher (0.6991).

client_side_cost_multipliers.detail: The site's JS applies a multiplier to *_cost_usd fields for a few models before display (gpt-5.6-luna x0.2, gpt-5.6-terra x0.8, gemini-3.6-flash x0.5, deepseek-v4-pro x0.25 on v1 only). claude-fable-5 has NO multiplier, so its raw artifact cost equals its displayed cost.

rank.note: Site's default homepage table shows a curated 18 of 25 models; Fable 5 is 3rd there and also 3rd when all 25 models are ranked by the same displayed-row rule.

notes: ALL numbers in this file are transcribed from DeepSWE's own published JSON artifacts; none are derived from a local run and none are estimated. Values marked null were genuinely not published.
The three requested task ids all exist in the DeepSWE v1.1 113-task set and all three have published claude-fable-5 results.

PER-TASK RESULTS ARE NOT SHOWN AS A SINGLE PASS/FAIL. Each task is run 4 times per reasoning effort (5 efforts x 4 runs = 20 attempts per task), so the published result is k-of-n. The 'all_efforts_pooled' block is what the site's heatmap view displays; the 'headline_config_max' block is the slice that corresponds to the headline leaderboard row.
None of the 73 excluded (model_routing_404) Fable-5 trials fell on any of the three target tasks - all 20 attempts are scored for each of them.

Fable 5's headline row uses reasoning_effort 'max' because the site picks the highest available effort, not the best score. Its 'xhigh' config actually scores marginally higher (0.6991 vs 0.6972) at ~62% of the cost ($13.41 vs $21.63). Quoting 'max' matches the site; quoting 'xhigh' would be the model's best published pass@1.

Fable 5 (0.697248) and gpt-5.6-terra (0.696231) are effectively tied for 3rd/4th; their confidence intervals overlap heavily. gpt-5.6-terra is not in the site's default 18-model table but is present in the underlying data.

The mean_input_tokens figures are cumulative across every agent step of a rollout (mini-swe-agent resends context each step), which is why they are in the millions. They are dominated by cache reads and are NOT comparable to a single-request input token count. Use median_peak_context_tokens for context-window comparisons.
DeepSWE's CI is a run-to-run SE across 4 whole-benchmark passes, not a binomial/Wilson interval over 113 tasks. A local harness reporting a Wilson interval is not directly comparable.

HARNESS MISMATCH: every DeepSWE number was produced with mini-swe-agent, a minimal single-agent scaffold - not claude-code or any plugin-based harness. Tool access, context management and prompting differ, so these are tier-placement context, not a like-for-like baseline.
The site publishes no per-task confidence intervals and no per-task figures for models other than the 8 in the heatmap artifact.
The site does not publish a dated/versioned API model string for Fable 5, only the short id 'claude-fable-5'. Provider recorded in the trial rows is 'vertex_ai'.

NOT AVAILABLE / recorded as null or omitted: per-task confidence intervals; any published aggregate for Fable 5 under v1 (v1 predates Fable 5 - it appears only in v1.1); a full API model identifier; and separate cache-write vs cache-read token accounting (only n_cache_tokens is given).
Reproduce by re-fetching the artifact URLs in 'fetched_from'; the artifacts are regenerated as new jobs land, so re-check 'artifact_generated_at' before reusing these numbers.
